Hi Alyssa / Jacob —

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for the time and for walking us through the HealthLytics demo flow. Per our call, I wanted to capture the open questions on data handling so your legal/security team has something concrete: 

Summary/asks from HealthLytics side (please confirm):
- Which prompt fields (free text, structured patient identifiers, attachments) does Redwood persist after inference completes?
- Are model outputs (generated text) written to logs or retained anywhere by default? If so, for how long and in what storage (S3, GCS, internal DB)?
- Are request traces / KV cache contents ever persistent or exportable?
- What options do you provide to opt out of storage or to shorten retention windows for hosted customers?
- Data residency: can you guarantee US-only storage for prompt and output artifacts for our account?

We have an upcoming security review on 9/2 where these answers will be required in writing. Could you please confirm the default behaviors and what can be changed for a Dedicated/Private deployment? I've attached our post-demo notes and would appreciate a short one-pager we can drop into the review packet.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood provides a short written summary (answer the bullets above) + one-pager by 8/24
2) Security deep-dive (60m) the week of 8/30; propose Tue 8/31 10am PT
3) If retention/export is possible, HealthLytics to provide exact audit log requirements so we can scope the implementation work

Thanks — Logan

Logan — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifying items from our side before your team drafts the write-up: 

- HealthLytics requires that any PII that appears verbatim in prompt inputs (names, SSNs, MRNs, PHI text) not be persisted beyond the processing window unless explicitly logged for auditing.
- We may need up to 90 days of audit logs showing request IDs, timestamps, and the (redacted) prompt hash. We cannot accept full prompt text in exported logs for patient identifiers.
- For model outputs: we need the option that outputs are never stored by the vendor; if Redwood must store outputs for debugging, we need a configurable opt-in / short retention policy (<=30 days).

Attached is our security questionnaire with the fields that will be queried in the review. If you can mark the items you can satisfy for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, that will help speed the process.

Can Marissa or Rishi confirm whether Redwood supports returning a stable prompt hash instead of the full text in logs, and whether KV cache is ever serialized to durable storage for Hosted customers?

Thanks, Alyssa

Hi Alyssa — looping in Rishi (applied ML/inference infra) and Laura (privacy/compliance) to address the technical and legal pieces. Below is a short, actionable summary you can include in your packet; happy to expand to a formal one-pager if that helps. Attachment: redwood-data-processing-matrix.xlsx (quick mapping).

Short answers (Hosted API default, unless customer requests otherwise):
- Prompt inputs: processed in-memory for inference; transient copies are kept for debugging and observability by default in aggregated logs. Default log retention: 30 days. Logs are stored in US regions for US customers.
- Model outputs: not persisted to long-term storage by default for streaming responses. Some debug traces may include generated text; those traces are part of the 30-day debugging logs and can be disabled.
- KV cache: never serialized to durable object storage for Hosted customers; it is ephemeral in the serving tier.
- Prompt hashing: we can provide ADR-friendly prompt hashing (SHA-256 of normalized prompt) in logs instead of the full prompt text for Hosted, and we can redact or replace tokens that match configured PII patterns prior to logging.
- Export/90-day audit log support: available for Dedicated deployments (can ship log exports up to 90 days). For Hosted, we can provide a 30-day export by default; longer retention requires Dedicated or Private.
- Opt-out and config: customers can request stricter retention and opt-out of debug logging (no prompt or output text) at the account level; for regulatory-controlled customers we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private which supports configurable retention, US-only residency, and customer-managed KMS.

Compliance artifacts / controls: SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA (link below); we support KMS (customer key) for Private and Dedicated.

Next steps (I volunteer to send a formal one-pager):
- Logan: please confirm you want the one-pager by 8/24 so I can include the Dedicated vs Hosted matrix.
- Alyssa: if 90-day audit logs are non-negotiable for Hosted, we should discuss Dedicated sizing and pricing in the security deep-dive.

Regards,
Marissa

Adding a quick technical point: for Hosted customers we do keep a short-lived immutable trace that contains a prompt hash + metadata (request_id, model_version, timestamps). The hash is deterministic for the normalized prompt; it is useful for replay/debug without sharing raw PII. If HealthLytics needs full 90-day traceability with exports of redaction metadata, Dedicated is the recommended path — we can provide S3-compatible export with the redacted artifacts and hashes.

I can demo the hashing/redaction flow in the security deep-dive.

-Rishi
